title: Superfast hole spin qubits enabled by uniaxial strain-boosted spin-orbit coupling
authors: Yi-Xu Wang, Yang Liu, Shan Guan, Jun-Wei Luo, Shu-Shen Li
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) electron/hole gases confined in semiconductor heterostructures suffer from weak Rashba spin-orbit coupling (SOC) for manipulating spin degreee of freedom via an electric rather than a magnetic field. Here, we show that complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor technology-accessible strain could substantially enhance the linear Rashba SOC of the top hole subband in Ge/SiGe quantum wells (QWs) to a level comparable to that of 2D Rashba materials through enhancing the mixture of the light-hole and heavy-hole bands. We further show that strongly enhanced Rashba SOC boosts the Rabi frequency of hole spin qubits confined in Ge/SiGe QWs by two orders of magnitude to an unprecedented 40 GHz, more than one order of magnitude faster than other qubit platforms. We also demonstrate that the hole spin rotation with Rabi frequency > 25 GHz enters a new regime being immune to gate control-induced electric noise, opening a new avenue to simultaneously improve the gate speed and gate fidelity. Our findings provide a new routine to substantially enhance the Rashba SOC in 2D semiconductor hole gases to a level that is great for spintronic applications.
summary: This paper demonstrates that applying uniaxial strain to Ge/SiGe quantum wells can dramatically enhance the Rashba spin-orbit coupling in 2D hole gases. This enhancement boosts the Rabi frequency of hole spin qubits to record-breaking speeds (40 GHz) while simultaneously creating an operational regime immune to electric noise, paving the way for faster, higher-fidelity solid-state quantum computation.
main_problem: The primary challenge is overcoming the inherently weak Rashba spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in 2D hole gases, which limits the speed and fidelity of electric-field-controlled spin manipulation for quantum computing applications.
main_result: The application of uniaxial strain, accessible via CMOS technology, can substantially enhance the linear Rashba SOC in Ge/SiGe quantum wells, boosting the hole spin qubit Rabi frequency to an unprecedented 40 GHz.
method: The study employs atomistic semi-empirical pseudopotential method (SEPM) calculations combined with model Hamiltonian analysis to theoretically predict the effect of strain on the SOC parameters.
model_or_system: The system involves hole spin qubits confined in Ge/SiGe quantum wells (QWs). The physics is governed by the effective SOC Hamiltonian, which is analyzed for its dependence on applied uniaxial and biaxial strain.
key_observables: Rabi frequency ($\omega_R$), linear Rashba SOC strength, single-qubit gate fidelity, and spin precession length.
important_parameters: Uniaxial strain ($\epsilon_u$), biaxial strain ($\epsilon_b$), and the vertical electric field ($E_z$).
main_assumptions: The enhancement mechanism is attributed to strain-induced heavy-hole-light-hole (HH-LH) mixing, which is otherwise symmetry-forbidden.
figures_summary: Figures compare qubit performance across platforms, illustrate the strain engineering approach by showing energy dispersion and SOC parameters ($\alpha_1, \alpha_2$) as functions of strain and electric field.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem of weak SOC, then details how strain engineering enhances the SOC parameters ($\alpha_1, \alpha_2$) using SEPM calculations. Finally, it demonstrates the resulting superfast qubit operation regime, including immunity to electric noise.
why_interesting: The work provides a concrete, material-science-based pathway (strain engineering) to enhance fundamental quantum coupling parameters (SOC) in solid-state systems, directly impacting the feasibility and speed of solid-state qubits.
